AntigravityOptionsModel.description:
Wire DTO for Antigravity CLI launch options (see :class:`AntigravityOptions`).

``model`` is free-form ``str`` — like the Claude/Codex DTOs — carrying the
full display name ``agy models`` prints (e.g. ``Gemini 3.1 Pro (Low)``);
the launcher forwards it verbatim as a single argv element.
``skip_permissions`` (``--dangerously-skip-permissions``) and ``sandbox``
are mutually exclusive — skip-permissions auto-approves ``bypassSandbox``
actions, silently defeating the sandbox (google-antigravity/antigravity-cli
#36) — so the combination is rejected with a 422 at the wire boundary. To
keep that guard airtight, ``model`` and each ``add_dirs`` entry (both
forwarded verbatim as argv elements) are rejected when they look like a CLI
flag (leading ``-``): otherwise a value such as
``add_dirs=["--dangerously-skip-permissions"]`` could smuggle the blocked
flag past the pair check. No legitimate value is affected — model names
start with a letter and directories with ``/`` or a drive letter.
``protected_namespaces=()`` silences pydantic's ``model_*`` guard for the
legitimately-named ``model`` field.
AntigravityOptionsModel.title: AntigravityOptionsModel

AutoScanFilterModel.description:
Per-project Linear filter for Auto Scan Mode.

Mirrors :class:`mobaide.core.projects_config.AutoScanFilter`. Validation:

* ``state_names`` and ``label_names`` must each contain at least one
  non-empty string. An empty list would silently match every issue,
  which is almost certainly not what the user wants — better to fail
  loud at the API boundary.
* ``active_state``, ``done_state``, ``removal_label`` must be non-empty.
AutoScanFilterModel.title: AutoScanFilterModel

ChatStoredSession.description: One session the agent stored on the host (``session/list``).
ChatStoredSession.title: ChatStoredSession

ClaudeOptionsModel.description:
Wire DTO for Claude CLI launch options (see :class:`ClaudeOptions`).

``effort`` is ``Literal``-typed so an invalid level is rejected with a 422 at
the wire boundary; ``model`` stays free-form (the client curates the alias
list). ``protected_namespaces=()`` silences pydantic's ``model_*`` guard for
the legitimately-named ``model`` field.
ClaudeOptionsModel.title: ClaudeOptionsModel

CodexLoginRequest.description:
API-key login payload.

The key is a :class:`pydantic.SecretStr` so it is auto-redacted in logs and
``repr``; it is piped to ``codex login --with-api-key`` via stdin and never
persisted by the agent (Codex writes its own ``auth.json``).
CodexLoginRequest.title: CodexLoginRequest

CodexOptionsModel.description:
Wire DTO for Codex CLI launch options (see :class:`CodexOptions`).

``sandbox`` and ``approval`` are ``Literal``-typed so an invalid value is
rejected with a 422 at the wire boundary rather than producing a broken
``codex`` argv. ``reasoning_effort`` is free-form like ``model``: the
vocabulary is enumerated per-model at runtime and advertised via
``capabilities.cli.codex.model_details``, so a closed Literal would 422
values the agent itself just advertised whenever the Codex catalog grows.
The value is embedded after ``=`` inside a single exec'd argv element
(``-c model_reasoning_effort=<v>``), so there is no flag-smuggling path.
``protected_namespaces=()`` silences pydantic's ``model_*`` guard for the
legitimately-named ``model`` field.
CodexOptionsModel.title: CodexOptionsModel

FsDirsResponse.description:
Subdirectory names of one host directory.

``path`` is the listed directory after ``~`` expansion, so a client that
completes ``~/co`` can write back an absolute path; on Windows its ``/``
separators are rewritten to ``\``, so a picked folder extends it with
the host's own separator. ``truncated`` means a scan cap or the time
budget stopped the listing early: the client must not filter it locally
as if it were complete, and re-asks with ``q``.
FsDirsResponse.title: FsDirsResponse

GitBranchCreateRequest.description:
``POST /branches``: create ``name`` at ``start_point`` (``HEAD`` of the
project root when omitted); ``checkout`` switches the project root to
it in the same call and is subject to the checkout refusals; ``force``
skips the busy-holder refusal after the user confirmed it.
GitBranchCreateRequest.title: GitBranchCreateRequest

GitBranchResponse.description:
Outcome of ``POST /branches`` and ``POST /checkout``: the local
branch touched, whether the project root now has it checked out and
whether the call created it.
GitBranchResponse.title: GitBranchResponse

GitCheckoutRequest.description:
``POST /checkout``: ``ref`` is a local branch name or a
``<remote>/<name>`` remote-tracking branch as listed by ``GET /items``;
a remote ref without a local branch of that name gets one created,
tracking it. ``force`` skips the busy-holder refusal after the user
confirmed it; every other checkout refusal still applies.
GitCheckoutRequest.title: GitCheckoutRequest

GitCommitContextResponse.description:
What the commit sheet needs before the user types: ``author`` is null
when git cannot determine an identity (the commit would be refused with
``identity_required``), ``head`` is null on an unborn branch (no amend).
GitCommitContextResponse.title: GitCommitContextResponse

GitConflictResolveRequest.description:
``content`` carries no length bound on purpose: a validation error
echoes its input, so the size is checked by the service instead.
GitConflictResolveRequest.title: GitConflictResolveRequest

GitConflictResponse.description:
A conflicted path as the resolver shows it. ``ours`` is index stage 2
and ``theirs`` stage 3 — during a rebase that is the branch being rebased
onto and the commit being replayed. ``kind`` is an open vocabulary:
``text`` | ``too_large`` | ``binary`` | ``encoding`` | ``missing`` |
``symlink`` | ``submodule`` | ``unsupported``; only ``text`` carries
``content`` (LF line endings, no BOM) and ``token``, the hash of the file
as read that ``resolve`` must send back.
GitConflictResponse.title: GitConflictResponse

GitConflictSide.description:
One side of a conflict. ``present`` is false when that side deleted
the file (or never had it); ``label`` names the side for the user and is
null when the agent cannot tell.
GitConflictSide.title: GitConflictSide

GitDeleteItem.description:
One item in a delete request.

The wire shape mirrors :class:`GitItemRead`'s discriminator — clients
echo back the ``kind`` and the appropriate identifier (``branch`` for
branch kinds, ``worktree_path`` for worktree kinds; both for combined
deletions). ``force`` upgrades a branch delete from ``-d`` to ``-D`` and
adds ``--force`` to a worktree removal so a worktree holding
modified/untracked files is deleted instead of refused.

``orphan_worktree`` removes only the worktree at ``worktree_path``,
whatever row it came from: sent for a ``branch_with_worktree`` row it
keeps the branch. ``remote_branch`` carries the row's ``branch``
(``<remote>/<name>``) verbatim and deletes that branch on the remote;
``force`` does not apply to it.
GitDeleteItem.title: GitDeleteItem

GitDeleteResultItem.description:
Per-item outcome.

``error`` codes:
    * ``force_required`` — branch is unmerged, or worktree holds
      modified/untracked files; retry with ``force=True``.
    * ``locked`` — worktree is locked.
    * ``not_found`` — branch or worktree no longer exists.
    * ``invalid`` — request payload missing the required identifier.
    * ``auth_required`` / ``network`` / ``remote_not_found`` — a
      ``remote_branch`` push could not reach or log in to the remote.
    * ``rejected`` / ``hook_failed`` — the remote, or a hook, refused
      the deletion.
    * ``git_timeout`` — the push outlasted its budget.
    * ``error`` — other git failure (full message in ``error_detail``).
GitDeleteResultItem.title: GitDeleteResultItem

GitItemRead.description:
One row in the unified git management list.

``branch`` is set for ``branch_*`` kinds and, as ``<remote>/<name>``,
for ``remote_branch``; ``worktree_path`` is set for
``branch_with_worktree`` and ``orphan_worktree``; ``remote`` only for
``remote_branch`` (remote and branch names may both contain ``/``, so
the client never splits ``branch`` itself). ``subject`` and
``committed_at`` (committer date, ISO 8601) describe the tip commit
when the ref resolves to one. Status fields apply where relevant;
clients should ignore irrelevant fields.
GitItemRead.title: GitItemRead

GitJobResponse.description:
One fetch/pull/push job: the body every job route answers and the
payload of both ``git.job.progress`` and ``git.job.done``. Every key is
always present; ``phase``/``percent``/``line`` mirror git's own
``--progress`` output, ``ok``/``error_code``/``message`` are null until
``status`` is ``done``. ``error_code`` is an open vocabulary (clients
render unknown codes from ``message``): ``cancelled`` | ``git_timeout``
| ``auth_required`` | ``network`` | ``remote_not_found`` | ``rejected``
| ``not_fast_forward`` | ``conflicts`` | ``dirty_worktree`` |
``unmerged`` | ``operation_in_progress`` | ``no_upstream`` |
``no_remote`` | ``detached_head`` | ``no_head`` | ``hook_failed`` |
``index_locked`` | ``git_error``.
GitJobResponse.title: GitJobResponse

GitPathsRequest.description:
Repo-relative paths as ``status`` reported them; a renamed entry lists
both ``path`` and ``orig_path``.
GitPathsRequest.title: GitPathsRequest

GitRebaseInfo.description:
The rebase in progress, read from git's state directory: ``branch`` is
null for a detached HEAD, ``onto_ref`` is a branch pointing at the base
(local first) or null, ``stopped_on`` is the commit git stopped at, and
``step``/``total`` count the todo list. Any key can be null — a rebase
git was killed in need not have written every file.
GitRebaseInfo.title: GitRebaseInfo

GitRebaseResponse.description:
Outcome of a rebase route. ``outcome`` is an open vocabulary:
``rebased`` | ``up_to_date`` | ``stopped`` | ``aborted``. ``rebase`` is set
only when ``stopped``; ``message`` is git's explanation of a stop that is
not a conflict (an untracked file in the way, an ``edit`` stop).
GitRebaseResponse.title: GitRebaseResponse

GitStatusEntry.description:
One row of the Changes list; a file that is both staged and modified
yields one entry per group.
GitStatusEntry.title: GitStatusEntry

GitUpstream.description: ``ahead``/``behind`` are null when the upstream ref no longer exists.
GitUpstream.title: GitUpstream

LinearLabelModel.description: Linear label discovered via the per-project API key.
LinearLabelModel.title: LinearLabelModel

LinearStateModel.description:
Linear workflow state discovered via the per-project API key.

``type`` is one of Linear's documented state types (``backlog`` /
``unstarted`` / ``started`` / ``completed`` / ``canceled`` / ``triage``).
Empty when the schema didn't include it (defensive — should not happen).
LinearStateModel.title: LinearStateModel

ProjectReadModel.description: Client-safe view of a single project.
ProjectReadModel.title: ProjectReadModel

ProjectUpdateModel.description:
Request body for ``PUT /api/projects/{name}``.

Three-state semantics for ``linear_api_key`` and ``conda_env`` follow the
GitHub/Stripe convention:

* field omitted / ``null`` → keep the existing value,
* empty string → clear (store ``None``),
* non-empty string → replace.

For ``default_flags``: ``null``/omitted keeps, a dict replaces the whole
map. Use ``{}`` to clear all flags.

For ``auto_scan_filter``: ``null``/omitted keeps; a model replaces
wholesale (no field-level merge — the whole filter is one logical unit).
ProjectUpdateModel.title: ProjectUpdateModel

SessionResponse.description:
REST response for a single session.

Field set is the canonical wire shape — must stay in lockstep with
:func:`mobaide.core.models.session_to_wire_dict` and the Android
``SessionResponse`` DTO. Add or rename a field in one place only.
SessionResponse.title: SessionResponse

VoiceCleanupRequest.description:
``kind`` is the session's kind: its CLI cleans up the text. Clients
from before ``cleanup_kinds`` send none and mean Claude Code.
VoiceCleanupRequest.title: VoiceCleanupRequest

VoiceCleanupResponse.description: The cleaned transcript; the original when there was nothing to clean.
VoiceCleanupResponse.title: VoiceCleanupResponse

VoiceCleanupSettingsRequest.description:
``PUT /api/voice/cleanup/settings``: turn transcript cleanup on or off
for every client of this agent.
VoiceCleanupSettingsRequest.title: VoiceCleanupSettingsRequest

VoiceStatusResponse.description:
``GET /api/voice/status`` and the ``voice.changed`` event payload.

``state``: ``unsupported`` | ``not_installed`` | ``queued`` |
``downloading`` | ``verifying`` | ``ready`` | ``failed``. ``progress`` is
set while ``downloading``; ``error`` while ``failed``; ``speed_factor``
(seconds of speech transcribed per second of CPU time, from the install
self-test) once ``ready``. ``repairing`` is true while an enabled voice
keeps its verified model and only needs its runtime again (after a
Python upgrade): cancelling then stops without deleting the model.
``cleanup_enabled`` is the user's transcript-cleanup choice for this
agent, shared by every client; it does not depend on the install state.
VoiceStatusResponse.title: VoiceStatusResponse

WorktreeBaseRef.description:
One branch a new worktree can start from. ``ref`` is what the client
sends back as ``base_branch``: a local branch name, or
``<remote>/<name>`` for a remote-tracking branch.
WorktreeBaseRef.title: WorktreeBaseRef

WorktreeBasesResponse.description:
``GET /worktree-bases``: the base-branch picker of the New Session
screen. ``default`` is the repository's default branch (``origin/HEAD``
first) and ``last_used`` the base of the last worktree created in this
project; both are ``null`` or a ``ref`` present in ``refs``. Clients
preselect ``last_used``, then ``default``.
WorktreeBasesResponse.title: WorktreeBasesResponse

post.description:
Trigger the staged-binary updater immediately, bypassing idle deferral.

Returns the updater outcome string verbatim (``"staged"``,
``"signature_failed"``, ``"no_change"``, ``"deferred"``) so the client
can surface a meaningful toast. On ``"staged"`` the supervisor restart
is scheduled as a FastAPI background task that runs *after* the HTTP
response is flushed, so the client receives the 200 reliably before
the agent exits with code ``EXIT_RESTART_REQUESTED``.

schema.title: Response Force Update Now Api Agent Update Force Now Post

post.description: Exchange a valid refresh token for a new token pair (rotation).
Validate credentials and return JWT access + refresh tokens.

Trigger an immediate scan cycle for a running auto scan.

Returns the freshly anchored ``next_scan_at`` so the caller can
rebind its countdown synchronously, without waiting for the bus event.
Start an auto scan for a project. 409 if already running, 429 if at cap.

schema.title: Response Start Scan Api Autoscan Start Post
Response Stop Scan Api Autoscan Stop Post

get.description:
Sessions the agent stored on this host, newest first.

Includes sessions started outside Mobaide, which a chat session can
continue (``chat_resume_id`` on create).

404.description: No chat agent of this kind

409.description: The agent cannot list its sessions

503.description: The agent cannot run on this host

post.description:
Authenticate the host's Codex CLI with an OpenAI API key.

Runs ``codex login --with-api-key`` as a one-shot subprocess with the key on
stdin (never argv, never persisted by us). The same configured binary and
``CODEX_HOME`` the launcher uses are applied, so the credential lands where
the create-session auth guard reads it.

get.description: Subdirectories of ``path`` for client-side path completion.

schema.title: Response List Projects Endpoint Api Projects Get

post.description: Create a new project. Returns 409 if the name is already taken.

patch.description: Atomically replace project ordering. 400 on set mismatch.

schema.title: Response Reorder Projects Endpoint Api Projects Order Patch

delete.description: Remove a project. 404 if unknown, 409 if a scan is active for it.

put.description:
Update a project. Supports rename via ``body.name``.

* 404 if ``name`` is unknown.
* 409 if renaming while an auto-scan is active for the old name, or if
  the new name collides with another existing project.

post.description:
Create a branch in the project's repository.

``400 bad_branch_name`` for a name git would refuse, ``409 exists`` /
``unknown_start_point`` for the obvious conflicts; with ``checkout``
the refusals of ``POST /checkout`` apply as well.

Check ``ref`` out in the project root.

Returns 409 with ``{busy_by: [...]}`` while a session or auto-scan work
item runs in the project root (a linked worktree's session does not
count) unless ``force`` is set, and a coded 409 — ``dirty``, ``checked_out_elsewhere``,
``operation_in_progress``, ``job_running`` — for the states git or the
agent refuse to switch in; ``404 ref_not_found`` for a ref that is
neither a local nor a remote-tracking branch.

get.description:
Return the unified list of local branches and worktrees, with the
remote-tracking branches appended when ``remote`` is set.

post.description:
Delete one or more branches/worktrees in a single batch.

Returns 409 with ``{busy_by: [...]}`` if any worktree in the batch is
held by a running session or auto-scan work item; the client should
surface a busy-conflict dialog and refuse to retry until the user
stops the holder. Per-item git failures (unmerged branch, locked
worktree, etc.) are returned in the 200 body so the user can act on
each row independently.

get.description: Return the base branches a new session's worktree can start from.

Return labels visible to the project's Linear API key, deduped by name.

Used by the Android project form to populate the multi-select chip
group for trigger labels and the dropdown for the removal label.

* 404 if the project is unknown.
* 400 if the project has no Linear API key.
* 502 if the upstream Linear API call fails.

schema.title: Response List Linear Labels Api Projects  Name  Linear Labels Get

get.description:
Return workflow states visible to the project's Linear API key.

Used by the Android project form to populate the multi-select chip
group for trigger states and the dropdowns for active / done states.

* 404 if the project is unknown.
* 400 if the project has no Linear API key.
* 502 if the upstream Linear API call fails.

schema.title: Response List Linear States Api Projects  Name  Linear States Get
Response List Sessions Api Sessions Get

get.description: Return the scrollback buffer for a session (for reconnection).

schema.title: Response Version Info Api Version Get
